_readme: Reviewed exemptions for backend/edgar/cik_reconcile.py. JSON has no comments,
so this key carries the rules.
WHY A LIST AT ALL. Two of the four buckets have a legitimate population.
A CIK can correctly have no companies row (an ETF, a trust, a holdco shell,
a predecessor CIK of a merged registrant), and a companies row can correctly
carry a CIK that owns no us-gaap facts (a foreign private issuer filing 20-F
or 40-F under IFRS, a closed-end fund, a listing that files nothing with SEC).
Reporting those alongside real orphans is how a check gets muted, and a muted
check is worse than no check because it also carries the belief that someone
is watching.
WHY IT IS NOT A BARE LIST OF NUMBERS. Every entry carries the evidence that
justified it and the date it was established. An exemption you cannot audit is
indistinguishable from a bug someone silenced. `forms` is what SEC's own
submissions index reported for that CIK on `reviewed_on`.
WHY IT CANNOT ROT. classify() audits this file against live data every run and
reports any entry that no longer describes a live condition, so an exemption
cannot outlive the situation it excused. Delete a spent entry the run it is
reported; do not leave it 'just in case'.
TO MAKE THE CHECK FIRE ON SOMETHING HERE: delete its object. That is the whole
procedure, and it is deliberately one line, because the cost of a wrong
exemption must stay lower than the cost of arguing about it.

no_company_row.reason: Unit investment trust, not an operating company. SEC entityType is 'investment' and it files only fund forms, so there is no issuer for a companies row to represent and no us-gaap financial statements to store.

no_facts.reason: 40-F filer under the Canadian MJDS. Reports under IFRS, publishes no us-gaap XBRL company facts, so financial_facts can never hold rows for it.
